questions.q: What are the three parts of a Terraform resource block's header?
options: A subscription ID, a resource group, and a region
Only a type and nothing else
The keyword `resource`, a version number, and a provider name
The keyword `resource`, the resource type, and a local name
questions.explain: resource "type" "local name" { ... } is the shape every resource block shares, regardless of what it provisions.

questions.q: What does the resource type (e.g. `azurerm_storage_account`) determine?
options: Exactly which Azure API this block maps to, as defined by the provider
The local name Terraform will assign automatically
Nothing -- resource type is purely cosmetic
Which region the resource will be created in
questions.explain: The resource type is defined by the provider (azurerm) and tells Terraform which specific Azure resource kind and API to call.

questions.q: How does Terraform know to create a resource group before a storage account that references it?
options: Terraform always creates resources in the order they're typed in the file, with no other logic
The storage account block references the resource group's attributes (e.g. azurerm_resource_group.example.name), and Terraform infers build order from that reference
You must manually write a numbered ordering block
It doesn't -- both resources are always created simultaneously
questions.explain: Terraform builds a dependency graph automatically from attribute references -- no explicit ordering syntax is needed.

questions.q: What is the difference between a resource's local name and its `name` attribute?
options: The local name is what Azure Portal displays; the name attribute is internal only
There is no difference -- they are the same value
They are always required to be identical strings
The local name only has to be unique within your .tf files and is never seen by Azure; the name attribute is the real Azure resource name
questions.explain: The local name scopes a block within your configuration; the name attribute is what actually gets created in Azure and, for some types, must be globally unique.

questions.q: Which resource type from this lesson is the same one covered by hand in DE Foundations Lesson 1?
options: azurerm_storage_account
azurerm_virtual_network
azurerm_key_vault
azurerm_resource_group
questions.explain: DE Foundations Lesson 1, "Azure Storage Accounts," had the student create this same resource type manually in the Portal.
